issue.title: get params segmentation fault
issue.body:
Hi, here are some questions when I using MAVSDK C++. I'm new to this, appreciated if helping me out 
- Use mavsdk::Telemetry plugin. When automatically retrieving certain parameters, such as "CAL_ACC0_ID", "CAL_MAG0_ID", a segmentation fault shows up. 
- Use mavsdk::Telemetry plugin. After receiving parammeters , trying to excute `mavsdk::TelemetryImpl::set_health_gyrometer_calibration(bool) ()` results in a instance of `std::system_error`
- Use mavsdk::Param plugin. When excuting `get_all_params()`, a `std::future_error `shows up.

## Environment

- MAVSDK version v1.4.13
- PX4 version v1.12.3

 ## Stacktrace

I subscribed the health messages simultaneously. When gps is active, the health message tells the local positon, global position and home position is all ok,. It seems under the circumstance, the sefmentation fault after retrieving "CAL_ACC0_ID", "CAL_MAG0_ID" can be observed, but the `std::system_error` not. I don't know if it's related, if not, just ignore this.

comments.body: Same issue [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1917). Author was unable to reproduce and we got around it by just using mavlink passthrough call to request all params. It's not as eloquent because we just use a timeout to determine when we've "should" have received all params. For us it was on startup connection so the delay in receiving the params was not an issue.

Thanks for the report.

> MAVSDK version: v1.4.0-418-gf7da49b4-dirty

Are you sure this is reproducible against v1.4.13? It looks like you're on a version based on something closer to the `main` branch. And note that I have recently refactored all of the param system in `main`, so this might be fixed if you use latest `main` (what is going to be v2 soon).

Sorry for not replying in time. 
I did get the wrong version. Recently I have tried both `v1.4.13` and `v1.4.16`,`get_allparams()` still got error, but latest main works.
For other problems, It was found that it was caused by the telemetry plugin being declared in a timer.

timeline.body: Same issue [here](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1917). Author was unable to reproduce and we got around it by just using mavlink passthrough call to request all params. It's not as eloquent because we just use a timeout to determine when we've "should" have received all params. For us it was on startup connection so the delay in receiving the params was not an issue.

Thanks for the report.

> MAVSDK version: v1.4.0-418-gf7da49b4-dirty

Are you sure this is reproducible against v1.4.13? It looks like you're on a version based on something closer to the `main` branch. And note that I have recently refactored all of the param system in `main`, so this might be fixed if you use latest `main` (what is going to be v2 soon).

Sorry for not replying in time. 
I did get the wrong version. Recently I have tried both `v1.4.13` and `v1.4.16`,`get_allparams()` still got error, but latest main works.

issue.title: get all parameters doesn't update values

repository.name: WayWise
repository.description: A rapid prototyping library for connected, autonomous vehicles developed at RISE Dependable Transport Systems

issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
Param::AllParams mavsdk::Param::get_all_params() doesn't retreive the updated values, but requests on specific parameter values with for example std::pair<Result, int32_t> get_param_int(std::string name) does.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Open ControlTower and RCCar
2. Click on 'Vehicle Parameters' and then 'Get Parameters From Vehicle'. Change a value and then click 'Set New...'. If you now click 'Get Param...' the list will update and your newly set value will return to old value

**Expected behavior**
Clicking 'Get Parameter...' should display the current values, including your newly changed one

**Screenshots**
![Screenshot from 2024-02-01 11-23-53](https://github.com/RISE-Dependable-Transport-Systems/WayWise/assets/76961018/e74955ed-10d1-44e9-ab10-2a99b40d6798)


**System (please complete the following information):**
 - Hardware: [Desktop]
 - OS: [Ubuntu Linux]
 - Version [22.04]

**Additional context**
Seems MAVSDK has had problems with the Param::AllParams mavsdk::Param::get_all_params() function for quite some time 
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1805
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2100

There has also been a refactoring lately
https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/1772

I made a temporary fix that's to be removed when this is resolved
https://github.com/RISE-Dependable-Transport-Systems/WayWise/commit/636d308a02d03c340fc8761ebfac627d44127961
